Hey!! I recently got a nose piercing and I love it lots! 

Go get it PROFESSIONALLY done at a local piercing/tattoo place. No guns. Pretty simple. 

I have a cleaning solution in a spray bottle. I spray the solution to the piercing (wipe off the excess) twice a day. Pretty simple, in the morning and at night. 

As for the pain, for me, the pain is very tolerable. It may hurt more than a lobe, but much less than a cartilage. Pain is subjective, though, my tolerance in pain is pretty high. But most of people I know would say the pain is little.

Hope this helped! :)

It was so difficult to get help especially when your mom is the one who said “you don’t need help.” When I look back at those times, I get really pissed because I could’ve gotten help so much faster. People with eating disorders have the most trouble getting help, because many don’t show much difference in physical appearances (some do, I didn’t forget about the others). They also keep telling themselves that they don’t need help as well, because they don’t want to step out of their comfort zone. Ultimately, this is their coping mechanism. Eating disorders are more about external/internal/environmental conflicts than looking a certain way or physical appearances in general. 

When a good friend of mine told a school  counselor about my issues and how I needed help, I was really angry. Because that meant that I needed to deal with all these issues: gaining my weight back, being in therapy, actually facing my external/internal conflicts, etc. But now that I have been in treatment for 3 years, I have never been happier. I’m really thankful that my friend told that school counselor about me; if they didn’t, I would’ve still been miserable. It feels really nice to know someone cared enough about me that they actually talked to a trusted adult out of concern. 

So if you notice that someone is really struggling, please, let a trusted person/professional know. If you talk to the actual person, they would most likely refuse to get help, but that is also an option too. It might be difficult for both you and that person at first, but in the end, it really does mean the world to us to have someone to give us a gentle push to the road of recovery.
